title: Giving by a counterparty’s circle in the days around the Board’s vote on its file
question: Do an organization and the people who work for it give to supervisors just before or just after the Board votes on its contract, grant or lease?
finding: No bunching shows. 40 organizations named as counterparty in 91 passed Board files gave, in their own name or through donors naming them as employer, 245 contributions to a voting supervisor’s own committees within a year either side of the final vote. 30 fall within 30 days of the vote; the same supervisors’ whole donor calendars put 26 there, so the count is no more than the calendar alone gives. In the 30 days before the vote: 17 against 14 expected; in the 30 days after: 13 against 13. The rows list the 15 organization-and-supervisor pairs with a contribution inside the 30 days, by amount.
how: For each passed contract, grant-agreement, lease or loan file with an outside counterparty, the final Board roll call (as the shared roll-call reader defines it) gives the day and the members who voted aye or no. Contributions are those to the member’s own candidate committees from the organization itself or from individuals who wrote it as their employer, matched by exact name after removing punctuation and company suffixes; public bodies, the City and employer entries such as “self” or “retired” are left out. Each contribution within 365 days either side of the vote is placed in a bin by days from the vote. The expected count for a bin gives each contribution the share of ALL that member’s contributions in the same two years that fall in the bin, so campaign seasons are taken into account. A contribution counts once for each file of the giver’s that the member voted on in the two years.
limits: An employee of a large employer is not the employer; most of these donors are staff giving on their own account, and nearly all the votes were unanimous. Exact-name matching misses organizations whose staff write a different name. Contributions come in clusters (one fundraiser, many cheques), so the chance statement is rougher than it looks. A contribution near a vote is permitted unless the giver is the contractor, one of its listed officers or owners, or (since 2023, for some contracts and permits) a party who gave more than $250; nothing in this list says any row is one of those.
